findings.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the current compilation. This matches the recorded decision that metadata types are deliberately not analysed and are reported by their defining assembly, so the silent drop is deliberate.

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic. A missing diagnostic for such a type is not a defect.

findings.claim: The wrapper also drops diagnostics with no location (Location.None) or a location in an unrelated tree, for example when MemberNeedsKey is created with a null location. Because it is installed on the shared reportDiagnostic, it applies to every diagnostic path, not just metadata symbols. Location-less diagnostics that were previously reported could now vanish. MsgPack004 and MsgPack003 were recently adjusted, so this could change what they report.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer tests for MsgPack003, MsgPack004 and MsgPack005 and look for any diagnostic that used Location.None or a null location and is now filtered out. See [L9] and [L10] on recent false-positive adjustments.

findings.claim: The README and MsgPack004.md add a user-facing statement that diagnostics about members of referenced-assembly types are reported by the defining assembly. This is consistent with [L8], but the README section is a new heading placed between the custom-formatter and MagicOnion sections, which is unrelated to its topic. The claim is also broader than what the code enforces, since the wrapper silently drops all non-compilation locations.

receipt_plan.detail: Check that the README wording matches [L8] and the ReportIfLocatedInCompilation behaviour, and that the section placement fits the document structure.
